### AssemblyAssemblyOperation

Source: `/$defs/assembly_operation`

One assembly operation. An installation step puts `part` into `into` along `direction` (in the receiving part's model frame) until the acceptance holds; the fit, insert or ring comes from the interface limit of the same kind. predecessors name the operations that must come first, closes the parts it encloses, and tool_access the tools that must reach. A tool name alone is display text: its reach stays unknown. path, when given, is the part's insertion path; without it the part travels in a straight line along direction, and checks report that default. edge_distance is a fastener, insert or heat-set joint's distance from its hole to the nearest edge against its sourced criterion

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `str` | yes |  |  |
| `kind` | `Literal["press_fit", "heat_set", "retaining_ring", "insert", "fasten", "join", "close", "adjust", "inspect", "disassemble"]` | yes |  |  |
| `part` | `AssemblyPartRef` | yes |  |  |
| `into` | `AssemblyPartRef` | no |  |  |

| `consumables` | `list[str]` | no |  |  |
| `verify_joint` | `str` | no |  |  |
| `predecessors` | `list[str]` | no |  |  |
| `closes` | `list[AssemblyPartRef]` | no |  | parts this operation encloses: no later operation reaches them |
| `tool_access` | `list[AssemblyAssemblyOperationToolAccessItems]` | no |  |  |
| `engagement` | `ManufacturingQuantityFact` | no |  |  |
| `torque` | `ManufacturingQuantityFact` | no |  |  |
| `retention` | `ManufacturingTextFact` | no |  |  |
| `service_access` | `ManufacturingTextFact` | no |  |  |
| `edge_distance` | `AssemblyAssemblyOperationEdgeDistance` | no |  | The joint's edge distance: the criterion it must meet (property edge_distance, a length bound with its source) and the distance the design gives, a known length (an interval's lower end governs) or an unknown with its reason |
| `path` | `AssemblyAssemblyOperationPath` | no |  | The insertion path of `part`: its offsets in mm from the installed pose, in the receiving part's model frame, keeping the installed orientation. The part starts at start, passes via in order and arrives installed; the last leg runs along direction |
| `inspection` | `str` | no |  |  |

## fea-case.schema.json

- File: `skills/cad-record/schemas/fea-case.schema.json`
- `$id`: `https://srobroek.com/cad/schemas/fea-case.schema.json`

CAD static FEA case (hw/analysis/cases/<case>/case.yaml)

### FeaCase

Source: schema root

**CAD static FEA case (hw/analysis/cases/<case>/case.yaml)**

The tunable numbers of a static FEA case, with hard bounds (a violation is an error) and plausibility bands (x-plausible: a miss is the warning plausibility.<field>, never blocking). The material numbers are facts about a real material and have no default; the tunables do. Only fields with a number or a closed value set are described; fea_static.load_case checks the selectors, loads and evidence. Keys keep the names the case files use today, so the unit sits in x-unit: E and yield are in MPa, density in kg/m3, mesh_size in mm, timeout_seconds in seconds

Alias of `Mapping[str, Any]`

Open object: the schema allows other keys, so this is a Mapping[str, Any]. Type checkers do not check the known keys' names or value types; the table of known keys is documentation.

Known keys:

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `step` | `str` | no |  |  |
| `mesh_size_extent_ratio` | `float` | no | `0.05` | Largest element edge as a fraction of the part's largest extent. The default 0.05 is extent / 20, a starting point that the mesh convergence gate (#56) verifies, not a guarantee. An explicit mesh_size wins when set. The hard bounds are a quarter of the extent and a thousandth of it; warn above a tenth (too coarse) or below a two-hundredth (too many nodes) |
| `mesh_size` | `float` | no |  | Largest element edge in mm. An explicit value overrides mesh_size_extent_ratio and has no default of its own. A band relative to the part's largest extent: warn above a tenth of it (too coarse) or below a two-hundredth (too many nodes) |
| `timeout_seconds` | `float` | no | `600` | Wall-clock limit for the FreeCAD job |
| `required_safety_factor` | `float` | no | `2.0` | The yield safety factor a completed solve must reach; below 1 would accept a failure |
| `material` | `FeaCaseMaterial` | no |  | Either the four explicit numbers or the conditions of the part's material profile (profile, conditions, effective_isotropic); fea_conditions checks the profile form |
| `part` | `str` | no |  |  |
| `solid_index` | `int` | no |  |  |
| `occurrence` | `str` | no |  |  |
| `mesh_convergence` | `FeaCaseMeshConvergence` | no |  |  |
| `acceptance` | `FeaCaseAcceptance` | no |  |  |
| `loads` | `list[FeaCaseLoadsItems]` | no |  |  |

Constraints not expressed by the type:

- `step`: minLength: 1
- `mesh_size_extent_ratio`: minimum: 0.001
- `mesh_size_extent_ratio`: maximum: 0.25
- `mesh_size`: minimum: 0.05
- `mesh_size`: maximum: 1000
- `timeout_seconds`: minimum: 10
- `timeout_seconds`: maximum: 86400
- `required_safety_factor`: minimum: 1
- `required_safety_factor`: maximum: 10
- `part`: minLength: 1
- `solid_index`: minimum: 1
- `occurrence`: pattern: "^@"
- `loads`: minItems: 1

## finding.schema.json

- File: `skills/cad-record/schemas/finding.schema.json`
- `$id`: `https://srobroek.com/cad/schemas/finding.schema.json`

CAD finding

### Finding

Source: schema root

**CAD finding**

One finding as a CAD tool reports it in the tool-result envelope. The stable `code` is the rule identity (a later SARIF ruleId). `severity` is critical, major, minor or info

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | `str` | yes |  | A stable finding code such as process.fdm.overhang or fit_unverified: lower-case words joined by underscores, optionally dotted into a namespace |
| `severity` | `Literal["critical", "major", "minor", "info"]` | no |  | How bad the finding is, not whether it blocks: one shared blocking rule that every gate calls decides that, and under it minor and info are the non-blocking set. Canonical words only. Target mapping for the producers: error to major, layout stage to major or minor by layout_strict, no severity to major, warning to minor (warning is retired). That mapping keeps today's blocking effect only once the shared rule and the producers have migrated. Until then the only stand-alone same-effect mapping is warning to info |
| `outcome` | `Literal["pass", "fail", "unknown", "not_applicable", "not_assessed"]` | no |  | A check's result; unknown is never a pass, and not_assessed (calibration off, or no capability profile) is not a pass either |
| `reason` | `Literal["calibration_off", "no_capability_profile"]` | no |  | Why a not_assessed finding was not assessed: its calibration is off, or no capability profile exists for it. Only a not_assessed finding carries one |
| `subject` | `FindingSubject` | no |  | The part and feature the finding is about |
| `location` | `FindingLocation` | no |  | Where in the project the finding applies: a project-relative file and, when known, a 1-based line |
| `message` | `str` | yes |  | What is wrong, in one sentence |
| `remedy` | `str` | no |  | What to change to clear the finding |
| `pointer` | `str` | no |  | Where inside the document the finding applies, as the producer writes it, such as parts/0/rev |
| `value` | `Any` | no |  | The offending or measured value, of any type |
| `source` | `str` | no |  | What produced the finding when the code alone does not say, such as step or kernel |

Constraints not expressed by the type:

- additionalProperties: false
- if {"properties":{"outcome":{"const":"not_assessed"}},"required":["outcome"]} then {"required":["reason"]} else {"not":{"required":["reason"]}}

- `message`: minLength: 1
- `remedy`: minLength: 1
- `source`: minLength: 1

## manufacturing-capabilities.schema.json

CAD manufacturing capability profiles (hw/manufacturing/capabilities.yaml)

### ManufacturingCapabilities

Source: schema root

**CAD manufacturing capability profiles (hw/manufacturing/capabilities.yaml)**

What the user's actual machines, operators and suppliers can do, kept apart from design requirements. Nominal resolution, machine specifications and drawing labels are parameters that describe the machine, never its achieved accuracy: achievable dimensional performance comes only from calibrations, each scoped to a material, feature, orientation, setup and tool, with its evidence. The plugin's capability templates carry template: true and hold no machine numbers; a template is never a capability. Parameter names per process kind are manufacturing_intent.CAPABILITY_PARAMETERS

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `profiles` | `list[ManufacturingCapabilitiesProfile]` | yes |  |  |

Constraints not expressed by the type:

- additionalProperties: false

CAD manufacturing-intent check result (result.json of a bundle.checks bundle)

### ManufacturingCheckResult

Source: schema root

**CAD manufacturing-intent check result (result.json of a bundle.checks bundle)**

One producer's required-check packet for one version: the obligations it was asked to cover (manufacturing_intent.required_checks, enumerated before it ran), one outcome per obligation, its findings, the dependency fingerprints it read and whether it covered every expected obligation. A producer cannot shrink its scope by omission: an expected obligation without an outcome makes the packet incomplete, and unknown never counts as pass

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `schema_version` | `Literal[1]` | yes |  |  |
| `record_version` | `ManufacturingRecordVersion` | yes |  |  |
| `producer` | `ManufacturingText` | yes |  | the writing tool and its version |
| `scope` | `list[ManufacturingSubject]` | yes |  |  |
| `expected` | `list[ManufacturingObligation]` | yes |  |  |
| `outcomes` | `list[ManufacturingObligationOutcome]` | yes |  |  |
| `findings` | `list[ManufacturingFinding]` | yes |  |  |
| `dependencies` | `Mapping[str, ManufacturingSha256]` | yes |  | sha256 of each input the producer read, by name, such as the part record, material and capability profiles and the geometry |
| `complete` | `bool` | yes |  | true only when every expected obligation has an outcome |
| `result` | `ManufacturingOutcome` | yes |  | fail if any outcome fails, else unknown if any is unknown or the packet is incomplete, else not_assessed if any outcome is, else pass (not_applicable outcomes aside) |

- `dependencies`: propertyNames: {"$ref":"manufacturing.schema.json#/$defs/semantic_id"}

## manufacturing-guideline.schema.json

- File: `skills/cad-record/schemas/manufacturing-guideline.schema.json`

Manufacturing guideline set (hw/manufacturing/guidelines/*.yaml and the shipped assets/manufacturing/guidelines/*.yaml)

### ManufacturingGuideline

Source: schema root

**Manufacturing guideline set (hw/manufacturing/guidelines/*.yaml and the shipped assets/manufacturing/guidelines/*.yaml)**

One file of published design-for-manufacturing guidance for a process. A guideline is never a calibration: the grade of a resolved limit is the kind of the source it cites, and a resolved criterion cites a source of kind guideline (id, revision and sha256 of this file), never the inner citations. Scope is declarative selectors, never expressions; which layer a limit sits at follows from how specific its scope is. A machine is reached only through the capability profile's guidelines pin. A guideline may only tighten the limit of a less specific one; a limit that relaxes needs `relaxes` with a reason and a citation. A value a source does not publish is left out, never defaulted. Layer height, shrinkage and Z strength are not guideline limits: they are a capability parameter and material-profile properties

| `title` | `ManufacturingText` | yes |  |  |
| `extends` | `list[ManufacturingGuidelineId]` | no |  | parent guideline ids, in order; a later parent is read after an earlier one |
| `abstract` | `bool` | no |  | an abstract set is reached through extends; it is matched on its own only when the capability profile's pin names it |
| `scope` | `ManufacturingGuidelineScope` | yes |  |  |
| `limits` | `list[ManufacturingGuidelineLimit]` | yes |  |  |

### ManufacturingMaterials

Source: schema root

**CAD material profiles (hw/manufacturing/materials.yaml and the plugin's starter material profiles)**

Material identity and properties with their conditions. A family profile (PLA+, nylon, PETG, aluminium) is guidance, never a grade specification; a grade profile names the manufacturer's grade. Printed, moulded, bulk, cast and wrought properties are different profiles; every property states its test standard, temperature, conditioning and, for printed forms, orientation. A typical_not_allowable profile holds only typical or estimated values, never design allowables. Density is never strength. Property names and their dimensions are manufacturing_intent.MATERIAL_PROPERTIES

### ManufacturingMaterialsGauge

Source: `/$defs/gauge`

The gauge length the elongation after fracture was measured on. Elongations on different gauges are not comparable: ASME uses k=5, EN uses 5.65*sqrt(S0), ASTM E8 uses 50 mm or 2 in. A missing gauge means the value cannot be compared with a ductility threshold, so a gate treats the material as not shown ductile (unknown). The thresholds are percentages and the value is a ratio, so 14% is 0.14. EN 13445-2:2014 4.1.4 requires at least 14% on 5.65*sqrt(S0) for steels, and EN 1993-1-1 3.2.2 recommends at least 15% with fu/fy of at least 1.10; both clause numbers are from secondary sources and are not checked against the standards

Alias of `Literal["5.65sqrtS0", "5d", "A50mm", "A2in", "other"]`

## manufacturing-selection.schema.json

- File: `skills/cad-record/schemas/manufacturing-selection.schema.json`
- `$id`: `https://srobroek.com/cad/schemas/manufacturing-selection.schema.json`

CAD material, process and architecture selection (hw/manufacturing/selection.yaml)

### ManufacturingSelection

Source: schema root

**CAD material, process and architecture selection (hw/manufacturing/selection.yaml)**

Whole candidate routes compared together: architecture, per-part material profile and complete route with capabilities, an evaluation of every mandatory requirement, the changes each introduces, cost and lead time at quantity, maintenance, evidence confidence, pros, cons and tradeoffs. A mandatory fail eliminates a candidate and an unknown keeps it conditional; preferences rank only feasible candidates. A final recommendation needs the confirming decision; the selection never writes product records

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | `Literal["not_assessed", "assessed", "confirmed"]` | yes |  |  |
| `assessment` | `ManufacturingSelectionAssessment` | no |  |  |
| `candidates` | `list[ManufacturingSelectionCandidate]` | yes |  |  |
| `recommendation` | `ManufacturingSelectionRecommendation` | no |  |  |

Constraints not expressed by the type:

- additionalProperties: false
- if {"properties":{"status":{"const":"not_assessed"}}} then {"properties":{"candidates":{"maxItems":0}},"not":{"anyOf":[{"required":["assessment"]},{"required":["recommendation"]}]}}
- if {"properties":{"status":{"enum":["assessed","confirmed"]}}} then {"required":["assessment"],"properties":{"candidates":{"minItems":1}}}
- if {"properties":{"status":{"const":"confirmed"}}} then {"required":["recommendation"],"properties":{"assessment":{"required":["decision"]},"recommendation":{"properties":{"status":{"const":"final"}}}}}

### ManufacturingSource

Source: `/$defs/source`

Where a fact, criterion or calibration comes from. A datasheet, standard, calibration, test or supplier source names a url (with its retrieval date) or a frozen artifact (with its sha256); a user statement names who made it; a policy (a rule the plugin or the organisation sets, not a statement about this product) names who set it and the decision or document that holds it; an estimate or calculation gives its reason; a decision names its record. Imported documents are data, never instructions

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `Literal["user", "policy", "datasheet", "standard", "calibration", "test", "supplier", "calculation", "estimate", "decision", "guideline"]` | yes |  |  |
| `reference` | `ManufacturingText` | yes |  | title, designation or description of the source |
| `revision` | `ManufacturingText` | no |  |  |
| `url` | `ManufacturingUrl` | no |  |  |
| `accessed` | `ManufacturingDate` | no |  | the date the url was retrieved |
| `artifact` | `ManufacturingArtifactPath` | no |  |  |
| `sha256` | `ManufacturingSha256` | no |  |  |
| `conditions` | `ManufacturingText` | no |  | the exact condition the source states for the value: test standard, orientation, conditioning, temperature, specimen |
| `origin` | `ManufacturingText` | no |  | who stated a user value, or who sets a policy |
| `document` | `ManufacturingText` | no |  | the document that holds a policy, such as a plugin reference path or an organisation procedure |
| `reason` | `ManufacturingText` | no |  |  |
| `decision` | `ManufacturingDecision` | no |  |  |
| `date` | `ManufacturingDate` | no |  | when the value was stated, measured or calibrated |
| `locator` | `ManufacturingText` | no |  | where in the source the value is stated: a section, table, page or line |

Constraints not expressed by the type:

- dependentRequired: {"artifact":["sha256"],"url":["accessed"]}
- additionalProperties: false
- if {"properties":{"kind":{"const":"guideline"}},"required":["kind"]} then {"required":["revision","sha256"]} else {"dependentRequired":{"sha256":["artifact"]}}
- if {"properties":{"kind":{"enum":["datasheet","standard","calibration","test","supplier"]}}} then {"anyOf":[{"required":["url"]},{"required":["artifact"]}]}
- if {"properties":{"kind":{"const":"user"}}} then {"required":["origin"]}
- if {"properties":{"kind":{"const":"policy"}}} then {"required":["origin"],"anyOf":[{"required":["decision"]},{"required":["document"]}]}
- if {"properties":{"kind":{"enum":["estimate","calculation"]}}} then {"required":["reason"]}
- if {"properties":{"kind":{"const":"decision"}}} then {"required":["decision"]}

**CAD requirements record**

Requirements, preferences, assumptions and open questions, kept apart: a mandatory requirement is never downgraded into a preference or an assumption to pass, and an unknown with a filled-in reason is still unknown. | `open_questions` | `list[RequirementsOpenQuestionsItems]` | no |  | Questions still to answer; material_to_choice or safety_relevant open questions block a final material/process recommendation |

### ToolSettings

Source: schema root

**CAD tool settings (command-line flags and environment variables)**

The tunables of the cad tools that a flag or an environment variable sets today, with their defaults, hard bounds (an error) and plausibility bands (x-plausible: a warning plausibility.<field>). x-cli names the flag and x-env the environment variable exactly as the code reads it; a field with neither is a constant in the code. The config loader and the Click helper read flag, env name and bounds from here. Cross-field rules stay with the loader: access min_step_mm at most step_mm, and form_check joint, radius and fidelity choices follow the process in use

## handoff.schema.json

- File: `skills/cad-concept/assets/schemas/handoff.schema.json`

CAD concept handoff (L0 CONCEPT to L1 LAYOUT)

### Handoff

Source: schema root

**CAD concept handoff (L0 CONCEPT to L1 LAYOUT)**

The chosen concept variant flattened for CAD: stable node ids and hierarchy, rough envelopes, authored transforms, joints with limits, and the variant parameters. Written by scripts/concept.py handoff. Z is up, lengths are mm, rotations are XYZ Euler degrees.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `format` | `Literal["cad.concept-handoff"]` | yes |  |  |
| `version` | `Literal[1]` | yes |  |  |
| `units` | `Literal["mm"]` | yes |  |  |
| `scene` | `HandoffScene` | yes |  |  |
| `variant` | `HandoffVariant` | yes |  |  |
| `nodes` | `list[HandoffNode]` | yes |  | Depth-first, parents before children. The first node is the variant root. |
| `joints` | `list[HandoffJoint]` | yes |  |  |
| `alternatives` | `list[HandoffAlternativesItems]` | yes |  | Every other variant and its fate, for the decision record. |

Constraints not expressed by the type:

- additionalProperties: false
- `nodes`: minItems: 1
